segments.text: This J E E Advanced example goes from a single absorption all the way to spin state and colour.
An octahedral d six complex shows one d to d absorption at five hundred nanometres, and its pairing energy is nineteen thousand per centimetre.
The splitting energy is one over the wavelength, which for five hundred nanometres works out to twenty thousand per centimetre.
In energy terms, h c over lambda gives about three point nine eight times ten to the minus nineteen joule per ion, which is roughly two hundred forty kilojoule per mole.
Look at the colour wheel: absorbing at five hundred nanometres, the complex appears red and turns out low spin.
Since the splitting energy at twenty thousand is just greater than the pairing energy of nineteen thousand, the field forces pairing, so the complex is low spin, t two g six.
With zero unpaired electrons, the moment is zero and the complex is diamagnetic.
The absorption at five hundred nanometres removes blue green from white light, so the eye sees the complement, which is red.

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips for VBT and CFT

board_events.text: The bonding traps that cost marks
Counting d electrons from the neutral atom instead of the ion: always apply the oxidation number first, so iron two is d six, not d eight.
If $d^n$ is wrong, every downstream answer $-$ spin, moment, colour, CFSE $-$ fails
Misjudging ligand field strength: halides and water are weak field and high spin, while cyanide, carbonyl, ammonia and en are strong or medium$-$strong.
Forcing pairing in tetrahedral complexes: because the tetrahedral gap is small, tetrahedral complexes are essentially always high spin.
Computing the moment from the wrong quantity: the spin$-$only formula uses the unpaired count, not the charge, the d count, or the coordination number.
Inverting the wavelength$-$gap link: a larger splitting means a shorter absorbed wavelength, so strong$-$field complexes absorb high$-$energy, short$-$wavelength light.

Pro$-$tip: run the one chain every time $-$ oxidation number, d count, ligand field, spin, unpaired count, moment $-$ and remember the tariff, minus nought point four in t two g, plus nought point six in e g.

segments.text: Let us close bonding with the traps that quietly cost marks.
First, counting d electrons from the neutral atom instead of the ion. Always apply the oxidation number first, so iron two is d six, not d eight.
Remember, if the d n count is wrong, every downstream answer, spin, moment, colour and stabilisation energy, fails.
Second, misjudging ligand field strength. Halides and water are weak field and high spin, while cyanide, carbonyl, ammonia and en are strong or medium strong.
Third, forcing pairing in tetrahedral complexes. Because the tetrahedral gap is small, tetrahedral complexes are essentially always high spin.
Fourth, computing the moment from the wrong quantity. The spin only formula uses the unpaired count, not the charge, not the d count, not the coordination number.
Fifth, inverting the wavelength and gap link. A larger splitting means a shorter absorbed wavelength, so strong field complexes absorb high energy, short wavelength light.

The pro tip: run the one chain every time, oxidation number, d count, ligand field, spin, unpaired count, moment, and remember the tariff, minus nought point four in t two g and plus nought point six in e g.
bonding को उन traps के साथ खत्म करते हैं जो चुपचाप marks ले जाते हैं।
पहला, ion की जगह neutral atom से d electrons गिनना। हमेशा पहले oxidation number apply करो, तो iron two है d six, d eight नहीं।
याद रखो, अगर d n count गलत है, तो हर downstream answer, spin, moment, colour और stabilisation energy, fail हो जाता है।
दूसरा, ligand field strength गलत आँकना। Halides और water weak field और high spin हैं, जबकि cyanide, carbonyl, ammonia और en strong या medium strong.
तीसरा, tetrahedral complexes में pairing force करना। चूँकि tetrahedral gap छोटा है, tetrahedral complexes लगभग हमेशा high spin होते हैं।
चौथा, moment को गलत quantity से compute करना। spin only formula unpaired count use करता है, charge नहीं, d count नहीं, coordination number नहीं।
पाँचवाँ, wavelength और gap के link को invert करना। बड़ा splitting मतलब छोटा absorbed wavelength, इसलिए strong field complexes high energy, short wavelength light absorb करते हैं।
pro tip: हर बार एक ही chain चलाओ, oxidation number, d count, ligand field, spin, unpaired count, moment, और tariff याद रखो, minus नौंट point four t two g में और plus नौंट point six e g में।

sections.title: Synergic bonding: the give-and-take of metal and CO

board_events.text: How does a zero-oxidation-state metal hold ligands?
In tetracarbonylnickel the nickel is in the zero oxidation state $-$ it has lost no electrons at all. So how does a neutral metal atom hold ligands together?
The answer is a two$-$way, mutually reinforcing bond called synergic bonding, like two neighbours who each give more the more the other gives back.

board_events.caption: The two opposing electron flows of a synergic bond

board_events.text: Flow one, ligand to metal: the carbon lone pair of carbon monoxide donates into an empty metal orbital $-$ an ordinary coordinate sigma bond.
Flow two, metal to ligand: the electron$-$rich metal pushes filled d density back into an empty antibonding pi star orbital of carbon monoxide $-$ the pi back$-$bond.
Each flow strengthens the other $-$ that mutual reinforcement is what makes the word synergic
Carbon monoxide is poisonous for exactly this reason: it binds the haemoglobin iron by this same mechanism, far more strongly than oxygen, and will not let go.

segments.text: <curious>Here is a real puzzle:</curious> how does a metal in the zero oxidation state manage to hold any ligands at all?
In tetracarbonylnickel the nickel is in the zero oxidation state, having lost no electrons whatsoever. So how does a neutral metal atom hold its ligands together?
The answer is a two way, mutually reinforcing bond called synergic bonding, like two neighbours who each give more the more the other gives back.
Look at the picture: two electron flows running in opposite directions between the metal and carbon monoxide.
Flow one is ligand to metal: the carbon lone pair of carbon monoxide donates into an empty metal orbital, an ordinary coordinate sigma bond.
Flow two is metal to ligand: the electron rich metal pushes filled d density back into an empty antibonding pi star orbital of carbon monoxide, the pi back bond.
Each flow strengthens the other, and that mutual reinforcement is exactly what earns the word synergic.
Carbon monoxide is poisonous for precisely this reason: it grips the haemoglobin iron by this same mechanism, far more strongly than oxygen, and simply will not let go.
<curious>यहाँ एक असली puzzle है:</curious> zero oxidation state वाला metal आख़िर कोई ligands पकड़ता कैसे है?
tetracarbonylnickel में nickel zero oxidation state में है, उसने कोई electrons खोए ही नहीं। तो एक neutral metal atom अपने ligands को साथ कैसे पकड़ता है?
जवाब है एक two way, mutually reinforcing bond जिसे synergic bonding कहते हैं, जैसे दो neighbours जो एक-दूसरे को जितना ज़्यादा देते हैं उतना ज़्यादा वापस मिलता है।
picture देखो: metal और carbon monoxide के बीच दो electron flows opposite directions में चल रहे हैं।
Flow one है ligand to metal: carbon monoxide का carbon lone pair एक empty metal orbital में donate करता है, एक ordinary coordinate sigma bond.
Flow two है metal to ligand: electron rich metal filled d density को carbon monoxide के एक empty antibonding pi star orbital में वापस push करता है, यही pi back bond.
हर flow दूसरे को strengthen करता है, और यही mutual reinforcement शब्द synergic को कमाता है।
carbon monoxide इसी वजह से poisonous है: ये haemoglobin के iron को इसी mechanism से पकड़ता है, oxygen से कहीं ज़्यादा strongly, और छोड़ता ही नहीं।

sections.title: The measurable consequence: a weakened C-O bond

board_events.text: Back-donation weakens the C-O bond
The density the metal pushes into carbon monoxide goes into an antibonding orbital of the carbon$-$oxygen bond, and filling an antibonding orbital weakens it.
So the metal$-$carbon bond gets stronger, gaining pi character, while the carbon$-$oxygen bond gets weaker and lengthens $-$ its bond order drops below that of free carbon monoxide.

board_events.text: This is confirmed experimentally: the carbon$-$oxygen infrared stretching frequency in a carbonyl is lower than in free carbon monoxide, and the more electron$-$rich the metal, the lower it falls.
It also explains why carbon monoxide is built for this job: its highest occupied orbital is a sigma orbital on carbon $-$ so it always binds through carbon $-$ with empty pi star orbitals just above.
A single small molecule thus offers a ready sigma donor and a ready pi acceptor side by side, exactly the two ingredients synergic bonding needs.
This is also why carbon monoxide sits at the very top of the spectrochemical series: pi acceptors give the largest splitting

segments.text: There is a beautiful, measurable consequence of all this back donation.
The density the metal pushes into carbon monoxide goes into an antibonding orbital of the carbon oxygen bond, and filling an antibonding orbital weakens it.
So the metal carbon bond gets stronger, gaining pi character, while the carbon oxygen bond gets weaker and lengthens. Its bond order drops a little below that of free carbon monoxide.
Look at the frequency ladder: free carbon monoxide is highest, a terminal carbonyl lower, and a bridging one lower still.
This is confirmed experimentally: the carbon oxygen infrared stretching frequency in a carbonyl is lower than in free carbon monoxide, and the more electron rich the metal, the lower it falls.

It also explains why carbon monoxide is built for this job. Its highest occupied orbital is a sigma orbital concentrated on carbon, which is why it always binds through carbon, with empty pi star orbitals sitting just above.
So a single small molecule offers a ready sigma donor and a ready pi acceptor side by side, exactly the two ingredients synergic bonding needs.
This is also why carbon monoxide sits at the very top of the spectrochemical series: pi accepting ligands produce the largest crystal field splitting.
इस सारे back donation का एक beautiful, measurable consequence है।
जो density metal carbon monoxide में push करता है वो carbon oxygen bond के एक antibonding orbital में जाती है, और antibonding orbital भरना उसे weaken कर देता है।
तो metal carbon bond stronger होता है, pi character पाकर, जबकि carbon oxygen bond weaker होकर lengthen होता है। इसका bond order free carbon monoxide से थोड़ा नीचे गिर जाता है।
frequency ladder देखो: free carbon monoxide सबसे ऊपर, terminal carbonyl नीचे, और bridging और भी नीचे।
ये experimentally confirmed है: carbonyl में carbon oxygen infrared stretching frequency free carbon monoxide से कम होती है, और metal जितना ज़्यादा electron rich, उतनी नीचे गिरती है।

ये भी explain करता है कि carbon monoxide इस काम के लिए क्यों बना है। इसका highest occupied orbital carbon पर एक sigma orbital है, इसीलिए ये हमेशा carbon से बंधता है, और empty pi star orbitals ठीक ऊपर बैठे होते हैं।
तो एक single small molecule एक ready sigma donor और एक ready pi acceptor साथ-साथ देता है, बिलकुल वो दो ingredients जो synergic bonding को चाहिए।
यही वजह है कि carbon monoxide spectrochemical series में सबसे ऊपर बैठता है: pi accepting ligands सबसे बड़ी crystal field splitting देते हैं।

sections.title: Classifying carbonyls and their structures

board_events.text: Homoleptic, nuclearity, terminal and bridging
A homoleptic carbonyl has only carbon monoxide ligands, like tetracarbonylnickel; a heteroleptic one has carbon monoxide together with other ligands.
A mononuclear carbonyl has one metal centre; a polynuclear one has two or more, forming when a single metal cannot reach the noble$-$gas count alone.

board_events.caption: Geometries of the common carbonyls

board_events.text: A terminal carbonyl binds one metal, while a bridging carbonyl spans two metals; mononuclear carbonyls have only terminal ones.
The structures follow the coordination number: tetracarbonylnickel is tetrahedral, pentacarbonyliron is trigonal bipyramidal, and hexacarbonylchromium is octahedral.
Decacarbonyldimanganese is two square$-$pyramidal units joined by a metal$-$metal bond with no bridge, while octacarbonyldicobalt has a metal$-$metal bond plus two bridging carbonyls.
A bridging carbonyl is weakened more, so it shows an even lower infrared frequency than a terminal one $-$ how chemists tell them apart

segments.text: Now let us classify the carbonyls and meet their structures.
A homoleptic carbonyl has only carbon monoxide ligands, like tetracarbonylnickel, while a heteroleptic one has carbon monoxide together with other ligands.
A mononuclear carbonyl has one metal centre, while a polynuclear one has two or more, forming when a single metal cannot reach the noble gas count on its own.
Look at the geometries: tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal, octahedral, and a dimetal case with a metal metal bond.
A terminal carbonyl binds just one metal, while a bridging carbonyl spans two metals, and mononuclear carbonyls have only terminal ones.
The structures follow the coordination number: tetracarbonylnickel is tetrahedral, pentacarbonyliron is trigonal bipyramidal, and hexacarbonylchromium is octahedral.
Decacarbonyldimanganese is two square pyramidal units joined by a metal metal bond with no bridge, while octacarbonyldicobalt has a metal metal bond plus two bridging carbonyls.
A bridging carbonyl is weakened more, so it shows an even lower infrared frequency than a terminal one, and that is how chemists tell the two apart.
अब carbonyls को classify करते हैं और उनकी structures से मिलते हैं।
एक homoleptic carbonyl में सिर्फ़ carbon monoxide ligands होते हैं, जैसे tetracarbonylnickel, जबकि heteroleptic में carbon monoxide दूसरे ligands के साथ होता है।
एक mononuclear carbonyl में एक metal centre होता है, जबकि polynuclear में दो या ज़्यादा, जो तब बनता है जब एक metal अकेले noble gas count तक नहीं पहुँच पाता।
geometries देखो: tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal, octahedral, और एक dimetal case metal metal bond के साथ।
एक terminal carbonyl सिर्फ़ एक metal से बंधता है, जबकि bridging carbonyl दो metals को span करता है, और mononuclear carbonyls में सिर्फ़ terminal वाले होते हैं।
structures coordination number को follow करती हैं: tetracarbonylnickel tetrahedral है, pentacarbonyliron trigonal bipyramidal, और hexacarbonylchromium octahedral.
Decacarbonyldimanganese दो square pyramidal units हैं जो metal metal bond से जुड़े हैं बिना bridge के, जबकि octacarbonyldicobalt में metal metal bond plus दो bridging carbonyls हैं।
एक bridging carbonyl ज़्यादा weaken होता है, इसलिए वो terminal से भी कम infrared frequency दिखाता है, और chemists इसी से दोनों को अलग पहचानते हैं।

sections.title: The EAN rule: chasing the krypton count

board_events.text: Effective Atomic Number and the eighteen-electron shell

Sidgwick's rule says a stable carbonyl tends to make the metal reach the electron count of the next noble gas, which for the first transition series is krypton, thirty six $-$ an eighteen$-$electron valence shell.
Here $Z$ is the metal's atomic number, each carbon monoxide donates two electrons, and a metal$-$metal bond contributes one electron to each metal.

board_events.text: Worked across the common carbonyls the pattern is striking: nickel, iron and chromium all reach thirty six with terminal carbon monoxide alone.
Manganese and cobalt fall one short as single metals, so they each form a metal$-$metal bond that supplies the missing electron.
The rule is a useful guide, not an absolute law $-$ hexacarbonylvanadium is a stable seventeen$-$electron exception

segments.text: Now the E A N rule, the metal's way of chasing the krypton count.

Sidgwick's rule says a stable carbonyl tends to make the metal reach the electron count of the next noble gas, which for the first transition series is krypton, thirty six, an eighteen electron valence shell.
The rule is: E A N equals Z minus the oxidation state, plus two times the number of donor atoms, plus one for each metal metal bond.
Here Z is the metal's atomic number, each carbon monoxide donates two electrons, and a metal metal bond contributes one electron to each metal.
Look at the table: every common carbonyl lands squarely on thirty six.
Worked across the common carbonyls the pattern is striking: nickel, iron and chromium all reach thirty six with terminal carbon monoxide alone.
Manganese and cobalt fall one short as single metals, so they each form a metal metal bond that supplies the missing electron.
The rule is a useful guide, not an absolute law. Hexacarbonylvanadium is a stable, isolable seventeen electron exception, one short of thirty six.
अब E A N rule, metal का krypton count chase करने का तरीक़ा।
Sidgwick's rule कहती है कि एक stable carbonyl metal को next noble gas के electron count तक पहुँचाता है, जो first transition series के लिए krypton है, thirty six, एक eighteen electron valence shell.
rule है: E A N बराबर Z minus oxidation state, plus two गुना donor atoms की संख्या, plus one हर metal metal bond के लिए।
यहाँ Z metal का atomic number है, हर carbon monoxide दो electrons donate करता है, और एक metal metal bond हर metal को एक electron देता है।
table देखो: हर common carbonyl ठीक thirty six पर लैंड करता है।
common carbonyls पर काम करने पर pattern striking है: nickel, iron और chromium सब सिर्फ़ terminal carbon monoxide से thirty six तक पहुँच जाते हैं।
Manganese और cobalt single metals के तौर पर एक short रह जाते हैं, इसलिए वो हर एक एक metal metal bond बनाते हैं जो missing electron देता है।
rule एक useful guide है, absolute law नहीं। Hexacarbonylvanadium एक stable, isolable seventeen electron exception है, thirty six से एक short.

board_events.text: The coordination number is four with sp3 hybridisation, so the geometry is tetrahedral.
Each metal$-$carbon bond is synergic: a sigma bond from the carbon lone pair of carbon monoxide donating into an empty nickel orbital, ligand to metal.
That sigma donation is reinforced by a pi back$-$bond, filled nickel d density donating into the empty antibonding pi star orbital of carbon monoxide, metal to ligand.
The two donations strengthen each other, which is exactly why a zero$-$oxidation$-$state metal can form a stable compound.
The back-bond is the whole point $-$ an answer without metal to pi star donation loses most marks

segments.text: This C B S E level example asks us to describe the metal carbon bond in tetracarbonylnickel, with the oxidation state and geometry of nickel.
Carbon monoxide is neutral and the complex is neutral, so nickel is in the zero oxidation state.
Look at the structure: four carbon monoxide ligands around nickel in a tetrahedral arrangement.
The coordination number is four with s p three hybridisation, so the geometry is tetrahedral.
Each metal carbon bond is synergic: a sigma bond from the carbon lone pair of carbon monoxide donating into an empty nickel orbital, ligand to metal.
That sigma donation is reinforced by a pi back bond, filled nickel d density donating into the empty antibonding pi star orbital of carbon monoxide, metal to ligand.
The two donations strengthen each other, which is exactly why a zero oxidation state metal can form a stable compound.
Remember, the back bond is the whole point. An answer without the metal to pi star donation loses most of the marks.

segments.text: This N E E T speed trap asks for the effective atomic number of iron in pentacarbonyliron, given that iron's atomic number is twenty six.
The speed logic: effective atomic number equals Z minus the oxidation number plus two times the carbon monoxide count.
So it is twenty six minus zero plus two times five, which is twenty six plus ten, giving thirty six.
Thirty six is the atomic number of krypton, so iron has attained a noble gas, eighteen electron configuration.
That is why pentacarbonyliron is stable, and why iron binds exactly five carbon monoxide ligands, because five is the number that reaches thirty six.
Look at the trigonal bipyramidal pentacarbonyliron sitting among the common structures.
The geometry is trigonal bipyramidal with d s p three hybridisation, following the coordination number of five.
The classic slip is counting one electron per carbon monoxide. Each one donates two, so it is two times five, not five.

sections.title: Worked example: why manganese forms [Mn2(CO)10]

board_events.text: An odd count forces a metal-metal bond
Manganese's atomic number is twenty five. For one manganese with $n$ terminal carbon monoxide, the count is twenty five plus two $n$.
To reach thirty six we would need two $n$ equal to eleven, so $n$ equals five point five $-$ impossible, since carbon monoxide ligands come in whole numbers.

board_events.text: With five carbon monoxide the count is twenty five plus ten, which is thirty five, one electron short of krypton.
Manganese solves this by forming a metal$-$metal bond with a second manganese pentacarbonyl unit; the shared bond contributes one electron to each manganese, giving thirty five plus one, thirty six.
The odd electron count of a single Mn(CO)5 fragment is exactly why dimerisation occurs

segments.text: This J E E Advanced example asks why manganese forms the dinuclear carbonyl rather than a mononuclear one, given its atomic number is twenty five.
Manganese's atomic number is twenty five. For one manganese with n terminal carbon monoxide, the count is twenty five plus two n.
To reach thirty six we would need two n equal to eleven, so n equals five point five, which is impossible, since carbon monoxide ligands come in whole numbers.
Look at the structure: two manganese pentacarbonyl units joined by a single metal metal bond.
With five carbon monoxide the count is twenty five plus ten, which is thirty five, one electron short of krypton.

Manganese solves this by forming a metal metal bond with a second manganese pentacarbonyl unit. The shared bond contributes one electron to each manganese, giving thirty five plus one, which is thirty six.
So the arithmetic is thirty five plus one from the metal metal bond, giving the krypton count of thirty six.
The odd electron count of a single manganese pentacarbonyl fragment is exactly why dimerisation occurs.
ये J E E Advanced example पूछता है कि manganese mononuclear की जगह dinuclear carbonyl क्यों बनाता है, यह देते हुए कि इसका atomic number twenty five है।
manganese का atomic number twenty five है। एक manganese के साथ n terminal carbon monoxide के लिए, count है twenty five plus two n.
thirty six तक पहुँचने के लिए हमें two n बराबर eleven चाहिए, तो n बराबर five point five, जो impossible है, क्योंकि carbon monoxide ligands whole numbers में आते हैं।
structure देखो: दो manganese pentacarbonyl units एक single metal metal bond से जुड़े हुए।
पाँच carbon monoxide के साथ count है twenty five plus ten, यानी thirty five, krypton से एक electron short.
manganese इसे दूसरे manganese pentacarbonyl unit के साथ एक metal metal bond बनाकर हल करता है। shared bond हर manganese को एक electron देता है, जिससे thirty five plus one, यानी thirty six.
तो arithmetic है thirty five plus one metal metal bond से, जो thirty six की krypton count देता है।
एक single manganese pentacarbonyl fragment का odd electron count ही वो वजह है जिससे dimerisation होता है।

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips for metal carbonyls

board_events.text: The carbonyl traps that cost marks
Describing only the sigma donation: the defining feature of carbonyl bonding is the back$-$bond, so an answer without metal to pi star donation and the word synergic loses most marks.
Assigning the metal a non$-$zero oxidation state: carbon monoxide is neutral, so in a homoleptic carbonyl the metal is almost always in the zero oxidation state.
Count two electrons per carbon monoxide in EAN, and add one per metal$-$metal bond for polynuclear carbonyls
Confusing terminal and bridging: decacarbonyldimanganese has no bridging carbonyl, while octacarbonyldicobalt does $-$ do not assume every polynuclear carbonyl is bridged.

Pro$-$tip: for any carbonyl, run the chain $-$ oxidation state usually zero, count the carbon monoxide, effective atomic number is $Z$ plus two times that, compare with thirty six, and if one short add a metal$-$metal bond.
For bonding descriptions, always write the two arrows explicitly: carbon to metal sigma, and metal to pi star carbon monoxide pi.

segments.text: Let us close carbonyls with the traps that cost marks.
First, describing only the sigma donation. The defining feature of carbonyl bonding is the back bond, so an answer without the metal to pi star donation and the word synergic loses most of the marks.
Second, assigning the metal a non zero oxidation state. Carbon monoxide is neutral, so in a homoleptic carbonyl the metal is almost always in the zero oxidation state.
Remember to count two electrons per carbon monoxide in the effective atomic number, and add one per metal metal bond for polynuclear carbonyls.
Third, confusing terminal and bridging carbonyls. Decacarbonyldimanganese has no bridging carbonyl, while octacarbonyldicobalt does, so never assume every polynuclear carbonyl is bridged.

The pro tip: for any carbonyl, run the chain. Oxidation state usually zero, count the carbon monoxide, effective atomic number is Z plus two times that, compare with thirty six, and if one short add a metal metal bond.
And for bonding descriptions, always write the two arrows explicitly: carbon to metal for the sigma, and metal to pi star carbon monoxide for the pi.
carbonyls को उन traps के साथ खत्म करते हैं जो marks ले जाते हैं।
पहला, सिर्फ़ sigma donation describe करना। carbonyl bonding की defining feature back bond है, इसलिए metal to pi star donation और synergic शब्द के बिना answer ज़्यादातर marks खो देता है।
दूसरा, metal को non zero oxidation state देना। carbon monoxide neutral है, इसलिए एक homoleptic carbonyl में metal लगभग हमेशा zero oxidation state में होता है।
याद रखो, effective atomic number में हर carbon monoxide के लिए दो electrons गिनो, और polynuclear carbonyls के लिए हर metal metal bond के लिए एक जोड़ो।

तीसरा, terminal और bridging carbonyls को confuse करना। Decacarbonyldimanganese में कोई bridging carbonyl नहीं, जबकि octacarbonyldicobalt में है, इसलिए कभी मत मानो कि हर polynuclear carbonyl bridged है।

pro tip: किसी भी carbonyl के लिए chain चलाओ। oxidation state usually zero, carbon monoxide गिनो, effective atomic number है Z plus two गुना वो, thirty six से compare करो, और अगर एक short हो तो metal metal bond जोड़ो।
और bonding descriptions के लिए, हमेशा दो arrows explicitly लिखो: carbon to metal sigma के लिए, और metal to pi star carbon monoxide pi के लिए।

sections.title: Stability as a position of equilibrium

board_events.text: A complex sits in a dynamic equilibrium
Drop a metal salt into a ligand solution and the complex that forms is not permanent $-$ it sits in equilibrium with the free metal ion and free ligands.

board_events.caption: The stability tug-of-war between free ions and the complex

board_events.text: Stability just measures how far that equilibrium lies towards the complex; a very stable complex has little tendency to fall back into its pieces.
The stability or formation constant, written K$_f$ or beta, is the scoreboard: a large value means the complex side wins decisively.
Because these constants span enormous ranges, we quote log K, so a complex with log K around twenty seven is overwhelmingly more stable than one near nine.
Thermodynamic stability (how far, K$_f$) is separate from kinetic stability (how fast ligands exchange, labile or inert)
A classic case: the tetracyanonickelate ion is very stable yet labile, while the hexammine cobalt three ion is only moderately stable yet kinetically inert.

segments.text: Let us start stability with a simple idea: a complex is not a permanent object, it sits in a dynamic equilibrium.
Drop a metal salt into a solution of ligands and the complex that forms is not permanent. It sits in equilibrium with the free metal ion and free ligands.
Look at the tug of war: on one side the free ion with its ligands, on the other the assembled complex.
Stability just measures how far that equilibrium leans towards the complex. A very stable complex has very little tendency to fall back into its pieces.
The stability, or formation, constant, written K f or beta, is the scoreboard for that tug of war. A large value means the complex side wins decisively.
Because these constants span enormous ranges, we quote log K. So a complex with log K around twenty seven is overwhelmingly more stable than one near nine.
And keep two ideas apart: thermodynamic stability is how far the equilibrium lies, measured by K f, while kinetic stability is how fast the ligands exchange, labile or inert.
A classic case: the tetracyanonickelate ion is thermodynamically very stable yet labile, while the hexammine cobalt three ion is only moderately stable yet kinetically inert.
stability की शुरुआत एक simple idea से करते हैं: एक complex permanent object नहीं है, ये एक dynamic equilibrium में बैठा होता है।
एक metal salt को ligands के solution में डालो और जो complex बनता है वो permanent नहीं है। ये free metal ion और free ligands के साथ equilibrium में रहता है।
tug of war देखो: एक तरफ़ free ion अपने ligands के साथ, दूसरी तरफ़ assembled complex.
Stability बस ये measure करती है कि वो equilibrium complex की तरफ़ कितना झुका है। एक बहुत stable complex का अपने pieces में वापस टूटने का बहुत कम tendency होता है।
stability, या formation, constant, जिसे K f या beta लिखते हैं, उस tug of war का scoreboard है। बड़ी value मतलब complex side decisively जीतती है।
चूँकि ये constants बहुत बड़ी ranges में फैले होते हैं, हम log K quote करते हैं। तो log K लगभग twenty seven वाला complex, nine के पास वाले से कहीं ज़्यादा stable है।
और दो ideas अलग रखो: thermodynamic stability है कि equilibrium कितना दूर लेटा है, K f से measure, जबकि kinetic stability है कि ligands कितनी तेज़ exchange होते हैं, labile या inert.
एक classic case: tetracyanonickelate ion thermodynamically बहुत stable है फिर भी labile, जबकि hexammine cobalt three ion सिर्फ़ moderately stable है फिर भी kinetically inert.

sections.title: The factors that raise or lower stability

board_events.text: Charge density, ligand nature, and the chelate effect
Factor one, charge density: the higher the charge and the smaller the metal ion, the more strongly it binds ligands, so iron three complexes beat the iron two ones.
Factor two, ligand nature: the more basic the ligand, or the higher it sits in the spectrochemical series, the more stable the complex $-$ cyanide beats ammonia beats water.

Factor five, the macrocyclic effect: a closed ring like a porphyrin is even more stable than an open-chain chelate of the same denticity

segments.text: Now the factors that decide whether a formation constant is large or small.
Factor one is charge density: the higher the charge and the smaller the metal ion, the more strongly it binds ligands, which is why iron three complexes are more stable than the iron two ones.
Factor two is the nature of the ligand: the more basic the ligand, or the higher it sits in the spectrochemical series, the more stable the complex, so cyanide beats ammonia beats water.
Look at the chelate picture: one bidentate en displaces two small molecules, and the number of free particles rises.
Factor three, the chelate effect, is the big one: a chelating ligand forms a far more stable complex than the same number of comparable monodentate ligands.
Why does it work? Releasing several small molecules when one chelate clamps on raises the disorder, so the positive entropy term drives the free energy more negative and beta larger.
Look at the Irving Williams curve: stability climbs across the row and peaks sharply at copper.
Factor four, the Irving Williams series: for the first row divalent ions with a given ligand, stability rises from manganese up to copper, peaking there, then dips at zinc.
And factor five, the macrocyclic effect: a closed ring like a porphyrin is even more stable than an open chain chelate of the same denticity.
अब वो factors जो decide करते हैं कि formation constant बड़ा है या छोटा।
Factor one है charge density: charge जितना ज़्यादा और metal ion जितना छोटा, उतनी strongly वो ligands बांधता है, इसीलिए iron three complexes iron two वालों से ज़्यादा stable होते हैं।
Factor two है ligand की nature: ligand जितना ज़्यादा basic, या spectrochemical series में जितना ऊपर, उतना stable complex, तो cyanide, ammonia को हराता है और ammonia, water को।
chelate picture देखो: एक bidentate en दो small molecules को displace करता है, और free particles की संख्या बढ़ जाती है।
Factor three, chelate effect, सबसे बड़ा है: एक chelating ligand उतने ही comparable monodentate ligands से कहीं ज़्यादा stable complex बनाता है।
ये काम क्यों करता है? जब एक chelate clamp करता है तो कई small molecules release होते हैं, disorder बढ़ता है, तो positive entropy term free energy को ज़्यादा negative और beta को बड़ा करता है।
Irving Williams curve देखो: stability row भर चढ़ती है और copper पर तेज़ी से peak करती है।
Factor four, Irving Williams series: first row divalent ions के लिए एक दिए ligand के साथ, stability manganese से copper तक चढ़ती है, वहाँ peak करती है, फिर zinc पर dip करती है।
और factor five, macrocyclic effect: porphyrin जैसा एक closed ring उसी denticity के open chain chelate से भी ज़्यादा stable होता है।

sections.title: Overall, stepwise, and the free-energy link

board_events.text: beta, the stepwise constants, and Delta-G
A complex with many ligands is built one ligand at a time, each addition having its own stepwise constant K one, K two, and so on.
Successive stepwise constants normally decrease, because each added ligand finds fewer vacant sites and faces more crowding.
A large beta means a large negative free$-$energy change, so log beta is essentially the free energy of formation on a logarithmic scale.

board_events.text: The instability, or dissociation, constant is simply the reciprocal, one over beta

segments.text: Now the quantitative tools: the overall constant, the stepwise constants, and the free energy link.
The overall constant beta is the concentration of the complex divided by the metal ion times the ligand concentration raised to n. A larger beta means a more stable complex.
A complex with many ligands is built one ligand at a time, and each addition has its own little equilibrium and its own stepwise constant, K one, K two, and so on.
The overall constant is the product of the stepwise constants, so the logarithms simply add: log beta equals log K one plus log K two and so on.
Successive stepwise constants normally decrease, because each added ligand finds fewer vacant sites and faces more crowding than the last.
The overall constant ties directly to free energy: Delta G standard equals minus R T natural log beta.
A large beta means a large negative free energy change, so log beta is essentially the free energy of formation written on a logarithmic scale.
Look at the copper table: log K climbs from water to ammonia to en to cyanide, exactly as ligand strength and chelation increase.
And note the flip side: the instability, or dissociation, constant is simply the reciprocal, one over beta.
अब quantitative tools: overall constant, stepwise constants, और free energy link.
overall constant beta है complex की concentration बटा metal ion गुना ligand concentration की n power. बड़ा beta मतलब ज़्यादा stable complex.
कई ligands वाला complex एक-एक ligand करके बनता है, और हर addition का अपना छोटा equilibrium और अपना stepwise constant होता है, K one, K two, वगैरह।
overall constant stepwise constants का product है, तो logarithms बस जुड़ते हैं: log beta बराबर log K one plus log K two वगैरह।
successive stepwise constants normally घटते हैं, क्योंकि हर added ligand को पिछले से कम vacant sites मिलती हैं और ज़्यादा crowding।
overall constant सीधे free energy से जुड़ता है: Delta G standard बराबर minus R T natural log beta.
बड़ा beta मतलब बड़ा negative free energy change, तो log beta essentially free energy of formation है, logarithmic scale पर लिखा हुआ।
copper table देखो: log K, water से ammonia से en से cyanide तक चढ़ता है, बिलकुल जैसे ligand strength और chelation बढ़ते हैं।
और flip side देखो: instability, या dissociation, constant बस reciprocal है, one over beta.

board_events.text: What a large log-beta actually means
The stability constant beta is the equilibrium constant for forming the complex from its metal ion and ligands.

board_events.text: A log beta of twenty one means beta is ten to the twenty one, an enormous number, so the equilibrium lies overwhelmingly toward the complex.
There is essentially no free silver ion left in solution, and the instability constant is its reciprocal, ten to the minus twenty one.
This is exactly why silver can be held in solution as this complex during electroplating and extraction $-$ the free silver is throttled to a trickle.
A large formation constant means a small dissociation constant: the complex barely comes apart

segments.text: This C B S E level example asks us to define the stability constant and interpret a large log beta for the silver dicyanido ion.
The stability constant beta is the equilibrium constant for forming the complex from its metal ion and its ligands.
For silver plus two cyanide going to the silver dicyanido ion, beta is the concentration of the complex over the silver ion times the cyanide concentration squared.
Look at the bars: a log beta of twenty one leaves almost no free silver on the reactant side.
A log beta of twenty one means beta is ten to the twenty one, an enormous number, so the equilibrium lies overwhelmingly toward the complex.
There is essentially no free silver ion left in solution, and the instability constant is its reciprocal, ten to the minus twenty one.
This is exactly why silver can be held in solution as this complex during electroplating and extraction: the free silver concentration is throttled down to a trickle.
So a large formation constant means a small dissociation constant. The complex barely comes apart.
ये C B S E level example हमसे stability constant define करने और silver dicyanido ion के लिए बड़े log beta को interpret करने को कहता है।
stability constant beta है complex को उसके metal ion और ligands से बनाने का equilibrium constant.
silver plus two cyanide से silver dicyanido ion बनने के लिए, beta है complex की concentration बटा silver ion गुना cyanide concentration का square.
bars देखो: twenty one का log beta reactant side पर लगभग कोई free silver नहीं छोड़ता।
twenty one का log beta मतलब beta है ten to the twenty one, एक enormous number, तो equilibrium overwhelmingly complex की तरफ़ लेटा है।
solution में essentially कोई free silver ion नहीं बचता, और instability constant इसका reciprocal है, ten to the minus twenty one.
यही वजह है कि silver को electroplating और extraction के दौरान इस complex के रूप में solution में रखा जा सकता है: free silver concentration एक trickle तक घटा दी जाती है।
तो बड़ा formation constant मतलब छोटा dissociation constant. Complex मुश्किल से टूटता है।

board_events.text: Speed logic: going from water to ammonia moves up the spectrochemical series, making it more stable.
Going from ammonia to en then adds the chelate effect, making it more stable still.
Answer: the bis-en copper complex $-$ the chelating ligand wins
The trap is thinking four ammonia beats two en because four is more than two.
Denticity, not ligand count, is what matters: two bidentate en clamp the metal in two chelate rings, and the entropy gain makes it more stable than four separate ammonias.

segments.text: This N E E T speed trap asks which copper complex is the most stable.
The candidates are the tetra aqua, the tetraammine, and the bis ethylenediamine copper two complexes.
Look at the copper bars again: log K rises steadily across these ligands.
The speed logic: going from water to ammonia moves up the spectrochemical series, which makes the complex more stable.
Going from ammonia to en then adds the chelate effect, making it more stable still.
So the answer is the bis en copper complex, because the chelating ligand wins.
The trap is thinking four ammonia beats two en, just because four is more than two.
Denticity, not the ligand count, is what matters: two bidentate en clamp the metal in two chelate rings, and the entropy gain makes the complex more stable than four separate ammonias.
ये N E E T speed trap पूछता है कि कौन सा copper complex सबसे stable है।
candidates हैं tetra aqua, tetraammine, और bis ethylenediamine copper two complexes.
copper bars फिर देखो: इन ligands पर log K steadily चढ़ता है।
speed logic: water से ammonia जाना spectrochemical series में ऊपर जाता है, जो complex को ज़्यादा stable बनाता है।
ammonia से en जाना फिर chelate effect जोड़ता है, जो इसे और भी ज़्यादा stable बनाता है।
तो answer है bis en copper complex, क्योंकि chelating ligand जीतता है।
trap ये है कि चार ammonia दो en को हरा देगा, सिर्फ़ इसलिए कि चार, दो से ज़्यादा है।
denticity, ligand count नहीं, वो चीज़ है जो matter करती है: दो bidentate en metal को दो chelate rings में clamp करते हैं, और entropy gain complex को चार अलग ammonias से ज़्यादा stable बनाता है।

sections.title: Worked example: stepwise to overall log-beta

board_events.text: Add the logs, do not multiply them in your head
A metal binds four ligands with stepwise constants log K one four point zero, log K two three point two, log K three two point five, and log K four one point eight.
So beta is ten to the eleven point five, which is about three point two times ten to the eleven.
Notice the stepwise values steadily decrease $-$ each successive ligand binds a little less favourably than the last.
The reasons are partly statistical, since fewer vacant sites remain, and partly steric and electronic, as the centre becomes less inviting.
A sudden rise in one stepwise K usually signals a structural change, such as octahedral switching to tetrahedral partway through

segments.text: This J E E Main example takes stepwise constants and builds the overall log beta.
A metal binds four ligands with stepwise constants: log K one four point zero, log K two three point two, log K three two point five, and log K four one point eight.
The overall log beta is simply the sum of the four stepwise logs.
Adding them: four point zero plus three point two plus two point five plus one point eight gives eleven point five.
So beta is ten to the eleven point five, which is about three point two times ten to the eleven.
Notice the stepwise values steadily decrease. Each successive ligand binds a little less favourably than the last.
The reasons are partly statistical, since fewer vacant sites remain for the next ligand, and partly steric and electronic, as the centre becomes less inviting.
And a sudden rise in one stepwise K usually signals a structural change, such as octahedral switching to tetrahedral partway through the series.
ये J E E Main example stepwise constants लेकर overall log beta बनाता है।
एक metal चार ligands बांधता है stepwise constants के साथ: log K one four point zero, log K two three point two, log K three two point five, और log K four one point eight.
overall log beta बस चारों stepwise logs का sum है।
जोड़ते हैं: four point zero plus three point two plus two point five plus one point eight देता है eleven point five.
तो beta है ten to the eleven point five, यानी लगभग three point two times ten to the eleven.
ध्यान दो stepwise values steadily घटती हैं। हर successive ligand पिछले से थोड़ा कम favourably बंधता है।
वजहें partly statistical हैं, क्योंकि अगले ligand के लिए कम vacant sites बचती हैं, और partly steric और electronic, क्योंकि centre कम inviting हो जाता है।
और किसी एक stepwise K में अचानक बढ़ोतरी usually एक structural change signal करती है, जैसे बीच में octahedral से tetrahedral switch होना।

A large beta throttles the free metal ion, which is the basis of masking in analytical chemistry

segments.text: This J E E Advanced example shows just how little free metal a big formation constant leaves behind.
The tetraammine zinc two ion has beta equal to ten to the nine. In a solution where the complex is nought point one zero molar and the free ammonia is one molar, we estimate the free zinc.
Start from beta equals the complex concentration over the zinc ion times ammonia to the fourth.
Rearranging, the free zinc is nought point one zero over ten to the nine times one to the fourth, which is one times ten to the minus ten molar.
Look at the bars: the complex is a tall column while the free zinc is a barely visible sliver.
The free zinc ion concentration is vanishingly small, about ten to the minus ten molar. Almost all the zinc is locked up in the complex.
This is exactly why complexation can stop a metal ion from giving its usual precipitation or qualitative analysis tests.
So a large beta throttles the free metal ion, and that is the basis of masking in analytical chemistry.
ये J E E Advanced example दिखाता है कि एक बड़ा formation constant कितना कम free metal छोड़ता है।
tetraammine zinc two ion का beta है ten to the nine. एक solution में जहाँ complex नौंट point one zero molar है और free ammonia one molar, हम free zinc estimate करते हैं।
beta बराबर complex concentration बटा zinc ion गुना ammonia की fourth power से शुरू करते हैं।
rearrange करने पर, free zinc है नौंट point one zero बटा ten to the nine गुना one की fourth power, यानी one times ten to the minus ten molar.
bars देखो: complex एक tall column है जबकि free zinc बमुश्किल दिखने वाला sliver.
free zinc ion concentration बहुत ही छोटी है, लगभग ten to the minus ten molar. लगभग सारा zinc complex में locked है।
यही वजह है कि complexation एक metal ion को उसके usual precipitation या qualitative analysis tests देने से रोक सकता है।
तो एक बड़ा beta free metal ion को throttle कर देता है, और यही analytical chemistry में masking का base है।

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips for stability

board_events.text: The stability traps that cost marks
Adding stepwise constants instead of multiplying: the overall beta is the product K one times K two and so on; it is the logarithms that add.
Mixing product and sum gives wildly wrong magnitudes $-$ work in logarithms and convert only at the end
Ranking stability by ligand count: two chelating en beat four monodentate ammonia, because denticity and the chelate effect, not the head$-$count, decide stability.
Confusing thermodynamic with kinetic stability: the formation constant measures how far the equilibrium lies, not how fast ligands exchange, so stable is not the same as inert.
Mixing up stability and instability constants: the instability constant is one over beta, so a large stability constant means a small instability constant.
Pro$-$tip: for which is most stable, run the three$-$factor scan $-$ metal charge density, then ligand field strength, then chelation $-$ and stop at the first factor that separates the candidates.

segments.text: Let us close stability with the traps that quietly cost marks.
First, adding stepwise constants instead of multiplying. The overall beta is the product, K one times K two and so on. It is the logarithms that add.
Remember, mixing the product and the sum gives wildly wrong magnitudes, so work in logarithms and convert to beta only at the very end.
Second, ranking stability by ligand count. Two chelating en beat four monodentate ammonia, because denticity and the chelate effect, not the head count, decide stability.
Third, confusing thermodynamic with kinetic stability. The formation constant measures how far the equilibrium lies, not how fast ligands exchange, so stable is not the same as inert.
Fourth, mixing up stability and instability constants. The instability constant is one over beta, so a large stability constant means a small instability constant.

The pro tip: for a which is most stable question, run the three factor scan, metal charge density, then ligand field strength, then chelation, and stop at the first factor that separates the candidates. Chelation almost always trumps the rest.
stability को उन traps के साथ खत्म करते हैं जो चुपचाप marks ले जाते हैं।
पहला, stepwise constants को multiply करने की जगह add करना। overall beta product है, K one गुना K two वगैरह। जुड़ते तो logarithms हैं।
याद रखो, product और sum मिलाने से magnitudes बुरी तरह गलत आती हैं, तो logarithms में काम करो और beta में सिर्फ़ आख़िर में convert करो।
दूसरा, stability को ligand count से rank करना। दो chelating en चार monodentate ammonia को हराते हैं, क्योंकि denticity और chelate effect, head count नहीं, stability decide करते हैं।

तीसरा, thermodynamic को kinetic stability से confuse करना। formation constant measure करता है कि equilibrium कितना दूर लेटा है, ना कि ligands कितनी तेज़ exchange होते हैं, तो stable, inert जैसा नहीं है।
चौथा, stability और instability constants मिलाना। instability constant है one over beta, तो बड़ा stability constant मतलब छोटा instability constant.

pro tip: which is most stable वाले सवाल के लिए three factor scan चलाओ, metal charge density, फिर ligand field strength, फिर chelation, और पहले ही factor पर रुको जो candidates को अलग करे। Chelation लगभग हमेशा बाक़ी सबको हरा देता है।

sections.title: Coordination compounds run the living and industrial world

board_events.text: Taking control of a metal ion
Everything so far $-$ Werner's spheres, ligands and chelates, isomerism, bonding, stability $-$ might feel abstract until you see that coordination compounds quietly run much of the world.
The green of every leaf, the red of your blood, a cancer drug, the way silver is pulled from rock, the chrome on a tap $-$ all of these are coordination chemistry at work.

board_events.caption: Every application is one idea: control the metal

board_events.text: A free metal ion is reactive and indiscriminate; wrap it in the right ligands and you can tune its colour, reactivity, solubility, even whether it gives a chemical test at all.
That control is exactly what makes these compounds useful, in biology and in industry alike.
The single idea threading through every application is one you already know: the chelate effect and the resulting high stability.
Usefulness needs the stability tuned for the job $-$ high enough to work, selective enough not to strip essential metals

segments.text: This final sub-topic is where the whole chapter pays off, so let us start with the big idea: taking control of a metal ion.

Everything so far, Werner's spheres, ligands and chelates, isomerism, bonding, stability, might feel abstract until you see that coordination compounds quietly run much of the living and industrial world.
The green of every leaf, the red of your blood, a cancer drug, the way silver is pulled from rock, the chrome on a tap, all of these are coordination chemistry at work.
Look at the map: every application is really one idea, taking control of a metal.
A free metal ion is reactive and indiscriminate. Wrap it in the right ligands and you can tune its colour, its reactivity, its solubility, even whether it gives a chemical test at all.
That control is exactly what makes these compounds useful, in biology and in industry alike.
The single idea threading through every application is one you already know: the chelate effect and the resulting high stability.
But usefulness needs the stability tuned for the job, high enough to work yet selective enough not to strip out essential metals.
ये final sub-topic वो जगह है जहाँ पूरा chapter pay off होता है, तो big idea से शुरू करते हैं: एक metal ion को control करना।

अब तक की हर चीज़, Werner की spheres, ligands और chelates, isomerism, bonding, stability, abstract लग सकती है जब तक आप ये न देखो कि coordination compounds चुपचाप living और industrial world का बहुत हिस्सा चलाते हैं।
हर पत्ते का हरा रंग, आपके खून का लाल, एक cancer drug, silver को चट्टान से निकालने का तरीक़ा, नल पर chrome, ये सब coordination chemistry हैं।
map देखो: हर application असल में एक ही idea है, एक metal को control करना।
एक free metal ion reactive और indiscriminate होता है। उसे सही ligands में लपेटो और आप उसका colour, reactivity, solubility, यहाँ तक कि वो chemical test देगा या नहीं, सब tune कर सकते हो।
यही control इन compounds को useful बनाता है, biology में और industry में भी।
हर application से गुज़रने वाला single idea वो है जो आप पहले से जानते हो: chelate effect और उससे मिलने वाली high stability.
पर usefulness के लिए stability काम के हिसाब से tuned होनी चाहिए, इतनी ज़्यादा कि काम हो पर इतनी selective कि essential metals न निकल जाएँ।

board_events.caption: The four biological metals as a memory set

board_events.text: That reversible coordination is what makes blood an oxygen courier $-$ and carbon monoxide is poisonous because it binds that same iron far more strongly and will not let go.
Vitamin B twelve is a coordination compound of cobalt, the anti$-$pernicious$-$anaemia factor, with cobalt held in a ring related to the porphyrins.
Metalloenzymes such as carboxypeptidase A and carbonic anhydrase carry a zinc ion at their active site

segments.text: Now the biggest showcase: coordination compounds in living systems, where a metal is held in a ring of donor atoms.
Look at the porphyrin: a metal locked at the centre of a nitrogen ring, held firmly but with a site left free.
Chlorophyll is a coordination compound of magnesium, the green pigment that captures light for photosynthesis, with its magnesium sitting inside a large nitrogen donor ring.
Haemoglobin is a coordination compound of iron, the red pigment of blood. The iron sits in a flat heme ring with a free sixth site to grip an oxygen molecule reversibly.
Look at the four biological metals as a memory set: magnesium, iron, cobalt and zinc.
That reversible coordination is exactly what makes blood an oxygen courier, and carbon monoxide is poisonous because it binds that same iron far more strongly and simply will not let go.
Vitamin B twelve is a coordination compound of cobalt, the anti pernicious anaemia factor, with cobalt held in a ring related to the porphyrins.
And metalloenzymes such as carboxypeptidase A and carbonic anhydrase carry a zinc ion right at their active site.
अब सबसे बड़ा showcase: living systems में coordination compounds, जहाँ एक metal donor atoms की एक ring में पकड़ा होता है।
porphyrin देखो: एक metal एक nitrogen ring के centre में locked, मज़बूती से पकड़ा हुआ पर एक site free छोड़ी हुई।
Chlorophyll magnesium का एक coordination compound है, हरा pigment जो photosynthesis के लिए light पकड़ता है, इसका magnesium एक बड़ी nitrogen donor ring के अंदर बैठा है।
Haemoglobin iron का एक coordination compound है, खून का लाल pigment. iron एक flat heme ring में बैठता है एक free sixth site के साथ जो एक oxygen molecule को reversibly पकड़ता है।
चार biological metals को एक memory set की तरह देखो: magnesium, iron, cobalt और zinc.
वही reversible coordination खून को एक oxygen courier बनाती है, और carbon monoxide poisonous है क्योंकि ये उसी iron को कहीं ज़्यादा strongly बांधता है और छोड़ता ही नहीं।
Vitamin B twelve cobalt का एक coordination compound है, anti pernicious anaemia factor, जिसमें cobalt porphyrins से related एक ring में पकड़ा है।
और carboxypeptidase A और carbonic anhydrase जैसे metalloenzymes अपने active site पर एक zinc ion रखते हैं।

board_events.caption: Only the cis isomer works as a drug

board_events.text: Cisplatin, the cis platinum ammine chloride, inhibits tumour growth in cancer chemotherapy $-$ and only the cis isomer is active, because it must bind two adjacent sites on a D N A strand.
Chelate therapy uses a chelating ligand to mop up a toxic metal and carry it out of the body: E D T A treats lead poisoning, and D$-$penicillamine and desferrioxamine remove excess copper and iron.
The art is selectivity: bind the toxic metal more tightly than the body's ligands, without stripping essential metals
In analysis, E D T A forms very stable one$-$to$-$one chelates, so it estimates calcium, magnesium and zinc quantitatively with a sharp end$-$point.
Water hardness is measured by titration with disodium E D T A, since calcium and magnesium form stable complexes and the volume used gives the hardness directly.
Selective complex formation gives characteristic tests: dimethylglyoxime gives a rosy$-$red complex with nickel, and the intense colours of transition$-$metal complexes allow colorimetric estimation.

segments.text: Now two applied fields that lean heavily on this chemistry: medicine and analytical chemistry.
Look at cisplatin: the cis form places its two chlorides adjacent, while the trans form cannot.
Cisplatin, the cis platinum ammine chloride, inhibits tumour growth in cancer chemotherapy, and only the cis isomer is active, because it must bind two adjacent sites on a D N A strand.
Chelate therapy uses a chelating ligand to mop up a toxic metal and carry it out of the body. E D T A treats lead poisoning, and D penicillamine and desferrioxamine remove excess copper and iron.
The art of it is selectivity: the drug must bind the toxic metal more tightly than the body's own ligands, without stripping out essential metals.
In analysis, E D T A forms very stable one to one chelates, so it estimates calcium, magnesium and zinc quantitatively with a sharp end point.
Water hardness is measured by titration with disodium E D T A, since calcium and magnesium form stable complexes, and the volume used gives the hardness directly.
And selective complex formation gives characteristic tests: dimethylglyoxime gives a rosy red complex with nickel, and the intense colours of transition metal complexes allow colorimetric estimation.
अब दो applied fields जो इस chemistry पर बहुत depend करते हैं: medicine और analytical chemistry.
cisplatin देखो: cis form अपने दोनों chlorides adjacent रखता है, जबकि trans form नहीं रख सकता।
Cisplatin, cis platinum ammine chloride, cancer chemotherapy में tumour growth रोकता है, और सिर्फ़ cis isomer active है, क्योंकि इसे एक D N A strand पर दो adjacent sites बांधने पड़ते हैं।

Chelate therapy एक chelating ligand का इस्तेमाल करके एक toxic metal को समेटकर शरीर से बाहर निकालती है। E D T A lead poisoning का इलाज करता है, और D penicillamine और desferrioxamine excess copper और iron निकालते हैं।
इसकी कला selectivity है: drug को toxic metal शरीर के अपने ligands से ज़्यादा tightly बांधना है, बिना essential metals निकाले।
analysis में, E D T A बहुत stable one to one chelates बनाता है, तो ये calcium, magnesium और zinc को एक sharp end point के साथ quantitatively estimate करता है।
Water hardness disodium E D T A से titration करके measure होती है, क्योंकि calcium और magnesium stable complexes बनाते हैं, और इस्तेमाल हुआ volume सीधे hardness देता है।

और selective complex formation characteristic tests देता है: dimethylglyoxime nickel के साथ rosy red complex देता है, और transition metal complexes के intense colours colorimetric estimation allow करते हैं।

board_events.caption: Extraction: dissolve as a stable complex, then release

board_events.text: Silver and gold are leached from their ores as soluble cyanide complexes, then recovered by displacement with a more reactive metal like zinc $-$ the cyanide process.
Nickel is purified by the Mond process: impure nickel is turned into volatile tetracarbonylnickel, which is then decomposed on heating to deposit pure nickel.
Electroplating with silver or gold uses complex baths, because the complex releases metal ions slowly and steadily, giving a fine, even, mirror$-$like deposit.
In photography, hypo, sodium thiosulphate, fixes the film by dissolving unexposed silver bromide as a soluble thiosulphate complex, so the image becomes permanent.
Coordination complexes are widely used as catalysts: Wilkinson's catalyst is a rhodium complex for hydrogenation, and Ziegler$-$Natta catalysts polymerise alkenes.
Prussian blue is an iron-cyanide pigment, and chelated iron E D T A feeds micronutrients to crops in agriculture

segments.text: Now the industrial sweep: metallurgy, plating, photography and catalysis, all running through complexes.
Look at the extraction cycle: dissolve the metal as a stable complex, then break the complex to set the metal free.
Silver and gold are leached from their ores as soluble cyanide complexes, then recovered by displacement with a more reactive metal like zinc. That is the cyanide process.
Nickel is purified by the Mond process: impure nickel is turned into volatile tetracarbonylnickel, which is then decomposed on heating to deposit pure nickel and regenerate the carbon monoxide.
Electroplating with silver or gold uses complex baths, because the complex releases metal ions slowly and steadily, giving a fine, even, mirror like deposit instead of a coarse one.
In photography, hypo, which is sodium thiosulphate, fixes the film by dissolving unexposed silver bromide as a soluble thiosulphate complex, so the image becomes permanent.
Coordination complexes are widely used as catalysts: Wilkinson's catalyst is a rhodium complex for hydrogenation, and Ziegler Natta catalysts polymerise alkenes to polythene and polypropene.
And a couple more: Prussian blue is an iron cyanide pigment, and chelated iron E D T A feeds micronutrients to crops in agriculture.
अब industrial sweep: metallurgy, plating, photography और catalysis, सब complexes से चलते हुए।
extraction cycle देखो: metal को एक stable complex के रूप में dissolve करो, फिर complex तोड़कर metal को free करो।
Silver और gold को उनके ores से soluble cyanide complexes के रूप में leach किया जाता है, फिर zinc जैसे ज़्यादा reactive metal से displacement करके recover किया जाता है। यही cyanide process है।

Nickel को Mond process से purify किया जाता है: impure nickel को volatile tetracarbonylnickel में बदला जाता है, जिसे फिर heat करके decompose करके pure nickel जमाया जाता है और carbon monoxide regenerate होता है।
Silver या gold से electroplating complex baths use करती है, क्योंकि complex metal ions धीरे और steadily release करता है, जिससे एक fine, even, mirror जैसा deposit मिलता है, coarse नहीं।
photography में, hypo, यानी sodium thiosulphate, film को fix करता है unexposed silver bromide को एक soluble thiosulphate complex के रूप में dissolve करके, तो image permanent हो जाती है।

Coordination complexes catalysts के तौर पर खूब use होते हैं: Wilkinson's catalyst hydrogenation के लिए एक rhodium complex है, और Ziegler Natta catalysts alkenes को polythene और polypropene में polymerise करते हैं।
और कुछ और: Prussian blue एक iron cyanide pigment है, और chelated iron E D T A agriculture में crops को micronutrients देता है।

sections.title: The logic behind every application

board_events.text: Why each application works, not just that it does

Why chelates dominate biology and medicine: a polydentate ligand wraps a metal in several rings, giving high stability, so nature holds a metal in place and medicine grabs a toxic metal tightly enough to excrete it.
Why cyanide extracts silver and gold: these noble metals will not dissolve, but cyanide turns them into stable, soluble complexes, and a more reactive metal then displaces them back out.
Why E D T A is the analyst's favourite: being hexadentate, it forms a single, very stable one$-$to$-$one chelate with almost any metal, giving a clean end$-$point and simple stoichiometry.

segments.text: This section is the payoff: not just that each application works, but why it works, which is far more memorable.

Why chelates dominate biology and medicine: a polydentate ligand wraps a metal in several rings, giving high stability, so nature holds a metal precisely in place and medicine grabs a toxic metal tightly enough to excrete it.
Why cyanide extracts silver and gold: these noble metals will not simply dissolve, but cyanide turns them into stable, soluble complexes, and a more reactive metal then displaces them back out.
Why E D T A is the analyst's favourite: being hexadentate, it forms a single, very stable one to one chelate with almost any metal, giving a clean end point and simple stoichiometry.
Look again at the map: one idea sits behind the whole list.

Why electroplating prefers complex baths: the complex holds the metal in equilibrium and releases free ions slowly, so the deposit is fine and even. The stability constant acts as a slow release valve.
Why complexes make good catalysts: a metal centre offers a vacant site to grab a reactant, activates it by donation and back donation, lets it react, then releases the product and cycles again.
So anchor every application to one idea: control of the metal through stable complex formation.
ये section असली payoff है: सिर्फ़ ये नहीं कि हर application काम करती है, बल्कि क्यों काम करती है, जो कहीं ज़्यादा याद रहता है।

chelates biology और medicine में क्यों छाए हैं: एक polydentate ligand metal को कई rings में लपेटता है, high stability देता है, तो nature एक metal को सही जगह रखती है और medicine एक toxic metal को इतना tightly पकड़ती है कि excrete कर दे।

cyanide silver और gold क्यों extract करता है: ये noble metals आसानी से dissolve नहीं होते, पर cyanide उन्हें stable, soluble complexes में बदल देता है, और फिर एक ज़्यादा reactive metal उन्हें वापस displace कर देता है।
E D T A analyst का favourite क्यों है: hexadentate होने से ये लगभग किसी भी metal के साथ एक single, बहुत stable one to one chelate बनाता है, जिससे clean end point और simple stoichiometry मिलती है।
map फिर देखो: पूरी list के पीछे एक ही idea बैठा है।

electroplating complex baths क्यों prefer करती है: complex metal को equilibrium में रखता है और free ions धीरे release करता है, तो deposit fine और even होता है। stability constant एक slow release valve की तरह काम करता है।

complexes अच्छे catalysts क्यों बनते हैं: एक metal centre एक vacant site देता है reactant पकड़ने के लिए, उसे donation और back donation से activate करता है, react होने देता है, फिर product release करके फिर cycle करता है।
तो हर application को एक idea से anchor करो: stable complex formation के ज़रिए metal का control.

segments.text: This J E E Main example reasons across topics: why cyanide extracts gold, and how the gold is recovered.
The question asks why gold, an unreactive metal, can be extracted using sodium cyanide, and how the dissolved gold is finally recovered.
Look at the two step logic: dissolve the gold as a stable complex, then break that complex to recover the metal.
Gold is too noble to dissolve directly, but cyanide ions convert it into the highly stable, water soluble gold dicyanido complex, and its large stability constant drives the dissolution.
The gold therefore passes into solution as a complex anion.
It is then recovered by displacement: adding a more reactive metal such as zinc reduces the complexed gold back to the free metal.
Complexation made the unreactive metal mobile, and a reactivity difference then set it free, the same strategy used to purify nickel in the Mond process.
So the pattern is: dissolve as a stable complex, then break the complex to recover the metal, a direct application of the stability ideas.
ये J E E Main example topics के आर-पार reason करता है: cyanide gold क्यों extract करता है, और gold कैसे recover होता है।
सवाल पूछता है कि gold, एक unreactive metal, sodium cyanide से क्यों extract हो सकता है, और dissolved gold आख़िर में कैसे recover होता है।
two step logic देखो: gold को एक stable complex के रूप में dissolve करो, फिर उस complex को तोड़कर metal recover करो।
Gold इतना noble है कि सीधे dissolve नहीं होता, पर cyanide ions इसे highly stable, water soluble gold dicyanido complex में बदल देते हैं, और इसका बड़ा stability constant dissolution drive करता है।
इसलिए gold एक complex anion के रूप में solution में चला जाता है।
फिर इसे displacement से recover किया जाता है: zinc जैसे ज़्यादा reactive metal डालना complexed gold को वापस free metal में reduce कर देता है।
Complexation ने unreactive metal को mobile बनाया, और फिर एक reactivity difference ने इसे free किया, वही strategy जो Mond process में nickel purify करने के लिए इस्तेमाल होती है।
तो pattern है: एक stable complex के रूप में dissolve करो, फिर complex तोड़कर metal recover करो, stability ideas का एक direct application.

board_events.caption: Only the cis isomer binds two adjacent DNA sites

board_events.text: The active compound is the cis platinum diammine dichloride, cis$-$diamminedichloridoplatinum two.
It works because its two labile chloride sites bind adjacent positions on D N A, and only the cis geometry places the two chlorides next to each other.
The trans isomer has them opposite and cannot make the same two$-$point attachment, so it is therapeutically useless $-$ a clinical consequence of geometrical isomerism.
A chelating drug for metal poisoning must bind the toxic metal more strongly than the body's own ligands, which needs a high stability constant.
But if it bound too strongly and indiscriminately it would strip out essential metals like zinc and calcium, so the stability must be high yet selective.
This ties the chapter together: structure identifies the species, bonding explains binding, stability decides whether it works as medicine

segments.text: This J E E Advanced example ties application, isomerism and stability together in one question.
Look at cisplatin: only the cis isomer places its two chlorides adjacent, ready to bridge to D N A.
The active compound is the cis platinum diammine dichloride, named cis diamminedichloridoplatinum two.
It works because its two labile chloride sites bind adjacent positions on a D N A strand, and only the cis geometry places the two chlorides next to each other.
The trans isomer has them opposite and cannot make the same two point attachment, so it is therapeutically useless, a clinical consequence of geometrical isomerism.
A chelating drug for metal poisoning must bind the toxic metal more strongly than the body's own ligands, which needs a high stability constant.
But if it bound too strongly and indiscriminately, it would strip out essential metals like zinc and calcium, so the stability must be high yet selective.
This ties the whole chapter together: structure identifies the species, bonding explains how it binds, and stability decides whether it will work as a medicine.
ये J E E Advanced example application, isomerism और stability तीनों को एक सवाल में जोड़ता है।
cisplatin देखो: सिर्फ़ cis isomer अपने दोनों chlorides adjacent रखता है, D N A से bridge करने को ready.
active compound है cis platinum diammine dichloride, जिसका नाम है cis diamminedichloridoplatinum two.
ये काम करता है क्योंकि इसके दो labile chloride sites एक D N A strand पर adjacent positions बांधते हैं, और सिर्फ़ cis geometry दोनों chlorides को अगल-बगल रखती है।
trans isomer में वो opposite होते हैं और वही two point attachment नहीं बना सकते, इसलिए वो therapeutically बेकार है, geometrical isomerism का एक clinical consequence.
metal poisoning के लिए एक chelating drug को toxic metal को शरीर के अपने ligands से ज़्यादा strongly बांधना होता है, जिसके लिए high stability constant चाहिए।
पर अगर वो too strongly और indiscriminately बांधे तो zinc और calcium जैसे essential metals निकाल देगा, इसलिए stability high पर selective होनी चाहिए।
ये पूरे chapter को जोड़ता है: structure species पहचानता है, bonding समझाता है कि कैसे बंधता है, और stability decide करती है कि ये medicine के तौर पर काम करेगा या नहीं।

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips for applications

board_events.text: The application traps that cost marks
Swapping the biomolecule and metal pairs: fix them as a set $-$ chlorophyll is magnesium, haemoglobin is iron, vitamin B twelve is cobalt, Wilkinson's catalyst is rhodium.
The iron and cobalt swap, blood versus vitamin, is the single most common error
Forgetting that only cisplatin is active: the anticancer activity is isomer$-$specific, so naming the trans isomer loses the point of the question.
Confusing the extraction and photography complexes: silver and gold extraction uses cyanide complexes, while photographic fixing uses the thiosulphate complex.

Listing applications without the reason: marks and understanding come from the why $-$ chelation and stability for biology and medicine, soluble complexes for extraction, slow ion release for plating.
Pro$-$tip: anchor every application to one underlying idea, control of the metal through stable complex formation, and you can reconstruct the example even if you forget the exact name.

segments.text: Let us close applications, and the chapter, with the traps that cost marks.
First, swapping the biomolecule and metal pairs. Fix them as a set: chlorophyll is magnesium, haemoglobin is iron, vitamin B twelve is cobalt, and Wilkinson's catalyst is rhodium.
The iron and cobalt swap, blood versus vitamin, is the single most common error here.
Second, forgetting that only cisplatin is active. The anticancer activity is isomer specific, so naming the trans isomer loses the whole point of the question.
Third, confusing the extraction and photography complexes. Silver and gold extraction uses cyanide complexes, while photographic fixing uses the thiosulphate complex.

Fourth, listing applications without the reason. Marks and understanding come from the why: chelation and stability for biology and medicine, soluble complexes for extraction, and slow ion release for plating.
The pro tip: anchor every application to one underlying idea, control of the metal through stable complex formation, and you can reconstruct the example even if you forget the exact name.
applications, और chapter, को उन traps के साथ खत्म करते हैं जो marks ले जाते हैं।
पहला, biomolecule और metal pairs बदल देना। इन्हें एक set की तरह fix करो: chlorophyll magnesium है, haemoglobin iron, vitamin B twelve cobalt, और Wilkinson's catalyst rhodium.
iron और cobalt का swap, blood बनाम vitamin, यहाँ सबसे common गलती है।
दूसरा, ये भूल जाना कि सिर्फ़ cisplatin active है। anticancer activity isomer specific है, तो trans isomer का नाम लेना सवाल का पूरा point खो देता है।
तीसरा, extraction और photography complexes को confuse करना। Silver और gold extraction cyanide complexes use करती है, जबकि photographic fixing thiosulphate complex.

चौथा, applications को बिना reason के list करना। Marks और understanding why से आते हैं: biology और medicine के लिए chelation और stability, extraction के लिए soluble complexes, और plating के लिए slow ion release.
pro tip: हर application को एक underlying idea से anchor करो, stable complex formation के ज़रिए metal का control, और आप exact नाम भूल भी जाओ तो example reconstruct कर सकते हो।

sections.title: Formula recap: the whole chapter on one page

board_events.text: Every working relation, gathered in one place
This recap restates the tools $-$ it does not re-teach them; return to the relevant sub-topic if any line feels unfamiliar

segments.text: Before the cheat sheet, let us gather every working relation from the whole chapter onto one page.
From Werner: the complex ion charge is the oxidation number plus the sum of ligand charges, and the coordination number is the sum of ligands times denticity.
From Valence Bond Theory: the spin only moment is root n into n plus two Bohr Magneton, where n is the number of unpaired electrons.
From Crystal Field Theory: e g sits at plus nought point six delta O, t two g at minus nought point four delta O, and the tetrahedral gap is four ninths of delta O.
The crystal field stabilisation energy is minus nought point four times the t two g count plus nought point six times the e g count, all times delta O, plus an m P term.
For spin and colour: delta O greater than P gives low spin, delta O less than P gives high spin, and delta O equals h c over lambda.
For carbonyls: the effective atomic number is Z minus the oxidation number plus two times the donor atoms, plus one per metal metal bond, aiming at thirty six.
For stability: beta is the complex over metal times ligand to the n, equal to the product of stepwise constants, and Delta G standard is minus R T natural log beta.
Remember, this recap restates the tools, it does not re-teach them, so return to the relevant sub-topic if any line feels unfamiliar.
cheat sheet से पहले, पूरे chapter की हर working relation को एक page पर इकट्ठा करते हैं।
Werner से: complex ion का charge है oxidation number plus ligand charges का sum, और coordination number है ligands गुना denticity का sum.
Valence Bond Theory से: spin only moment है root n into n plus two Bohr Magneton, जहाँ n unpaired electrons की संख्या है।
Crystal Field Theory से: e g बैठता है plus नौंट point six delta O पर, t two g minus नौंट point four delta O पर, और tetrahedral gap four ninths of delta O है।
crystal field stabilisation energy है minus नौंट point four गुना t two g count plus नौंट point six गुना e g count, सब गुना delta O, plus एक m P term.
spin और colour के लिए: delta O, P से बड़ा तो low spin, delta O, P से छोटा तो high spin, और delta O बराबर h c over lambda.
carbonyls के लिए: effective atomic number है Z minus oxidation number plus two गुना donor atoms, plus one हर metal metal bond के लिए, target thirty six.
stability के लिए: beta है complex बटा metal गुना ligand की n power, बराबर stepwise constants का product, और Delta G standard है minus R T natural log beta.
याद रखो, ये recap tools को restate करता है, दोबारा नहीं सिखाता, तो अगर कोई line unfamiliar लगे तो relevant sub-topic पर वापस जाओ।
